200	But first, we need to add one more point: we will read this Parashah
201	this year on a very important date.
202	Today is the 19th of Marcheshvan, which means that Shabbat, when we read Parashat Vayera,
203	what will the date be?
204	The 20th of Marcheshvan.
205	What is special about the 20th of Marcheshvan?
206	In recent generations the special quality of this day was revealed, beyond the hints in its
207	name.
208	The letter Kaf hints at Keter, the crown, the crown of the whole month of Marcheshvan, with
209	all its deep meanings. But in recent generations the special quality of this day was revealed: it is
210	the birthday of the Rebbe, whose soul is in Eden, as the fifth Rebbe is called
211	in the Chabad dynasty, whose name was Rabbi Shalom Dovber, or
212	in short, the Rebbe Rashab. The Rebbe Rashab was born
213	one hundred and sixty-six years ago, in the year
214	5621, on the 20th of Marcheshvan.
215	And when a Rebbe, who is the head of the Jewish people, is not a tzaddik for himself alone, but a tzaddik
216	who influences all the sons and daughters of Israel wherever they are, when his mazal is strong, his birthday
217	is the time when his mazal is strong, and so it influences all the people of Israel.
218	Yes, and so also the entire universe.
219	And then the question arises: what is the connection between "Vayera elav HaShem," between
220	the revelation that took place with the Holy One, blessed be He, with Avraham Avinu, the revelation of the Holy One, blessed be He, and
221	the matter of the birth of the Rebbe Rashab?
222	So as an introduction to all this, we need to tell a story that...
223	happened with the Rebbe himself, Rabbi Shalom Dovber, when he was a small child, a
224	well-known story, on his birthday, at the age of four or five years,
225	when his grandfather, the Tzemach Tzedek, was still alive in this world,
226	and he, the grandson, went in to the grandfather.
227	A birthday is a fitting and special time to go in to receive a blessing
228	from the Rebbe, from the grandfather who was the Rebbe, the Tzemach Tzedek.
229	The Rebbe Rashab was four or five years old.
230	For the grandfather, the Tzemach Tzedek, passed away when he was five and a half.
231	So here, when we speak about Parashat Vayera, about the day of
232	his birth, it is the age of four or five years.
233	And so the little grandson, the little child, went in to the Rebbe,
234	the grandfather, and begins to cry.
235	And what is he crying about?
236	He says, why did the Holy One, blessed be He, appear to Avraham Avinu, "Vayera elav HaShem,"
237	and to us He does not appear?
238	So what does the grandfather answer him?
